design: Proposal: accept any four-byte unsigned frame length and immediately read and allocate the entire JSON body. A length above 16 MiB is an ordinary frame, not a protocol violation; preserve the connection and require existing clients to accept it too. No versioning or interoperability work is needed because the length prefix itself is unchanged.

answer_key.defect: Accepting oversized frames breaks the framing contract: an oversized prefix is a protocol violation and the daemon closes without reading its body; an existing peer cannot be assumed to accept the proposed frame.
answer_key.evidence: WIRE.md:37-40 defines the four-byte prefix and the 16 MiB maximum, violation, and connection close before body read.

answer_key.defect: Allocating directly from an unchecked peer-supplied length removes the documented size bound and allows a single frame to demand up to the four-byte prefix limit, risking memory exhaustion.
answer_key.evidence: WIRE.md:37-38 defines both the peer-controlled prefix and the 16 MiB bound that the proposal removes.

checks: Sending oversized frames to a live service or changing the protocol implementation is unsafe.
